questions.explanation: Acquisition strategy risks should be identified in the planning phase, before contracting, so that they can shape requirements and the approach.
optionNotes: The follow-on phase covers sustainment after acquisition
Correct: acquisition risks are identified during planning
Acceptance is too late to identify these risks
Contracting acts on the risks already identified

questions.stem: Which of the following open source software issues pose the MOST risk to an application?
options: The software is beyond end of life and the vendor is out of business.
The software is not used or popular in the development community.
The software has multiple Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) and only some are remediated.
The software has multiple Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) but the CVEs are classified as low risks.
questions.explanation: Known vulnerabilities that remain unremediated are directly exploitable and so pose the greatest risk.
optionNotes: EOL is risky, but 'vendor' rarely applies to open source; the risk is less direct
Low popularity is an indirect risk
Correct: known, unremediated vulnerabilities are exploitable
Low-severity CVEs pose less risk

questions.stem: An organization is implementing security review as part of system development. Which of the following is the BEST technique to follow?
questions.explanation: Security review integrated into development works best as incremental assessments at each phase or iteration. Problems are found early, when they are cheapest to fix, instead of only at the end.
optionNotes: A third party could do reviews but isn't a technique for integrating them.
Architecture review is only one point in time.
Correct: continuous, phase-by-phase review fits the SDLC.
Penetration testing comes late and misses design flaws.

questions.stem: What are the roles within a scrum methodology?
options: Scrum master, retirements manager, and development team
System owner, scrum master, and development team
Scrum master, quality assurance team, and scrum team
Product owner, scrum master, and scrum team
questions.explanation: Scrum defines three roles: the product owner, the scrum master and the development (scrum) team.
optionNotes: 'Retirements manager' is not a Scrum role.
'System owner' is not a Scrum role.
QA is not a separate Scrum role.
Correct: product owner, scrum master and team.

questions.stem: Why should Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Application Security Verification standards (ASVS) Level 1 be considered a MINIMUM level of protection for any web application?
options: ASVS Level 1 ensures that applications are invulnerable to OWASP top 10 threats.
Opportunistic attackers will look for any easily exploitable vulnerable applications.
Most regulatory bodies consider ASVS Level 1 as a baseline set of controls for applications.
Securing applications at ASVS Level 1 provides adequate protection for sensitive data.
questions.explanation: ASVS Level 1 is the minimum for every application because opportunistic attackers scan widely for easy, known weaknesses. Level 1 covers exactly those low-hanging vulnerabilities.
optionNotes: Nothing makes an application invulnerable.
Correct: it defends against opportunistic attackers.
Regulators generally don't mandate ASVS Level 1.
Sensitive data needs Level 2 or 3.

questions.stem: Which programming methodology allows a programmer to use pre-determined blocks of code and consequently reducing development time and programming costs?
questions.explanation: Object-oriented programming promotes reuse of predefined classes and objects. Reuse shortens development time and lowers cost.
optionNotes: Application security is not a methodology for reusing code.
Correct: OOP enables reusable code blocks.
'Blocked algorithm' is not such a methodology.
Assembly is low-level and doesn't encourage reuse.

questions.stem: In order for application developers to detect potential vulnerabilities earlier during the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), which of the following safeguards should be implemented FIRST as part of a comprehensive testing framework?
questions.explanation: Threat modelling happens at design time, before code exists, so vulnerabilities are found earliest and cheapest. It also guides the later code review and testing.
optionNotes: Code review comes after coding.
Acceptance testing is late in the cycle.
Correct: it is the earliest safeguard, at the design stage.
Automated testing needs code to exist first.

questions.stem: When reviewing the security logs, the password shown for an administrative login event was ' OR ' '1'='1' --. This is an example of which of the following kinds of attack?
questions.explanation: ' OR '1'='1' -- is a classic SQL injection payload. It makes the WHERE clause always true and comments out the rest of the query, bypassing authentication.
optionNotes: Brute force tries many real passwords.
Correct: this is a SQL tautology injection.
XSS injects script into pages.
Rainbow tables crack password hashes.

questions.stem: A user's credential for an application is stored in a relational database. Which control protects the confidentiality of the credential while it is stored?
options: Validate passwords using a stored procedure.
Allow only the application to have access to the password field in order to verify user authentication.
Use a salted cryptographic hash of the password.
Encrypt the entire database and embed an encryption key in the application.
questions.explanation: A salted hash keeps the stored password unreadable even if the database is compromised, and the salt defeats precomputed rainbow tables. Embedding the encryption key in the application exposes it, and a stored procedure or field permissions do not protect the value itself.
optionNotes: A stored procedure controls how passwords are checked, not how they are stored.
Permission limits fail if the database is breached; the password stays readable.
Correct: a salted one-way hash protects stored credentials.
A key embedded in the app can be extracted, which undermines the encryption.

questions.stem: In a DevOps environment, which of the following actions is MOST necessary to have confidence in the quality of the changes being made?
options: Prepare to take corrective actions quickly.
Receive approval from the change review board.
questions.explanation: In DevOps, changes ship often through a CI/CD pipeline. Automated functional tests give fast, repeatable assurance that each change works. Manual board approval is too slow for that pace, and reviewing logs or preparing fixes happens after the fact.
optionNotes: Reactive; it does not build confidence before release.
A change board slows DevOps and does not test quality.
Log review is detective and happens after deployment.
Correct: automated testing gives continuous quality assurance.

questions.stem: The development team has been tasked with collecting data from biometric devices. The application will support a variety of collection data streams. During the testing phase, the team utilizes data from an old production database in a secure testing environment. What principle has the team taken into consideration?
options: Separate biometric data streams require increased security.
Biometric data must be protected from disclosure.
questions.explanation: By using real production biometric data only inside a secured test environment, the team is protecting that data from disclosure. Biometric data is highly sensitive personal data. The other statements do not explain the secure environment.
optionNotes: True of biometrics, but not the principle shown here.
Multiple streams are not what drives the secure environment.
The devices are not described as unknown.
Correct: the sensitive data must be protected from disclosure.

questions.stem: What testing technique enables the designer to develop mitigation strategies for potential vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: Threat modeling identifies potential threats and vulnerabilities at design time so the designer can plan mitigations. Penetration tests and code reviews find flaws after the code is written.
optionNotes: Inspections catch defects but are not structured for planning mitigations.
Pen testing happens after build and exploits existing flaws.
Correct: threat modeling drives mitigation design.
Code review finds implementation bugs after coding.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST method to validate secure coding techniques against injection and overflow attacks?
options: Scheduled team review of coding style and techniques for vulnerability patterns
Using automated programs to test for the latest known vulnerability patterns
The regular use of production code routines from similar applications already in use
Ensure code editing tools are updated against known vulnerability patterns
questions.explanation: Automated testing tools such as DAST scanners and fuzzers check code against known injection and overflow patterns consistently and at scale. Manual style reviews are less reliable, reusing code proves nothing, and editor updates are not validation.
optionNotes: Manual review is inconsistent and limited.
Correct: automated tools validate against known vulnerability patterns.
Reused code may carry the same flaws.
Editor updates do not validate the code.

questions.stem: Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software presents which of the following additional security concerns?
options: Vendors take on the liability for COTS software vulnerabilities.
In-house developed software is inherently less secure.
Exploits for COTS software are well documented and publicly available.
COTS software is inherently less secure.
questions.explanation: Widely deployed COTS products attract public research, so known exploits are documented and readily available to attackers.
optionNotes: Vendors generally disclaim liability via license terms.
Not a COTS-specific concern; source of software doesn't make in-house inherently weaker.
Correct: broad installed base means public, documented exploits.
Overgeneralisation; COTS isn't inherently less secure.

questions.stem: Which of the following techniques BEST prevents buffer overflows?
questions.explanation: Of the choices, reviewing code for unchecked bounds is the effective preventive technique; other options are meaningless.
optionNotes: Not a real technique; meaningless distractor.
Encoding doesn't enforce buffer bounds.
Correct: auditing code finds missing bounds checks.
Variable typing alone does not prevent overflow.

questions.stem: When auditing the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) which of the following is one of the high-level audit phases?
questions.explanation: Audits begin with planning, followed by fieldwork and reporting; planning is a high-level audit phase.
optionNotes: Requirements is an SDLC phase, not an audit phase.
Risk assessment is done within planning, not a top-level phase.
Due diligence is not an audit phase.
Correct: audits proceed planning, fieldwork, reporting.

questions.stem: A developer is creating an application that requires secure logging of all user activity. What is the BEST permission the developer should assign to the log file to ensure requirements are met?
questions.explanation: Append-only permission lets the app add log entries without altering or deleting existing ones.
optionNotes: Read-only cannot record activity.
Execute is irrelevant for a log.
Write allows overwriting/deleting entries.
Correct: append-only adds entries without altering history.

questions.stem: An application developer receives a report back from the security team showing their automated tools were able to successfully enter unexpected data into the organization's customer service portal, causing the site to crash. This is an example of which type of testing?
questions.explanation: Negative testing feeds invalid or unexpected input to check error handling.
optionNotes: Non-functional covers performance/usability, not invalid input.
Positive testing uses valid inputs.
Performance testing measures load, not bad input.
Correct: negative testing uses unexpected input.

questions.stem: An organization recently suffered from a web-application attack that resulted in stolen user session cookie information. The attacker was able to obtain the information when a user's browser executed a script upon visiting a compromised website. What type of attack MOST likely occurred?
questions.explanation: A malicious script executing in the victim's browser and stealing cookies is XSS.
optionNotes: Correct: script running in victim browser stealing cookies is XSS.
XXE targets XML parsers server-side.
SQLi targets the database.
CSRF forges requests, doesn't run scripts to steal cookies.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of web-based attack is happening when an attacker is able to send a well-crafted, malicious request to an authenticated user without the user realizing it?
questions.explanation: CSRF makes an authenticated user's browser send a forged request without their knowledge.
optionNotes: XSS injects script, not forged requests.
Correct: CSRF forges requests via the authenticated user.
Not a standard attack name.
Concerns weak session handling, not forged requests.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be included in a good defense-in-depth strategy provided by object-oriented programming for software deployment?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation hides an object's internal data and implementation behind defined interfaces, which limits exposure and supports layered defense.
optionNotes: Database/MLS technique, not an OOP feature
Lets objects respond differently; not a security layer
Right: data hiding protects internals
Reuse mechanism that can spread flaws

questions.stem: A financial organization that works according to agile principles has developed a new application for their external customer base to request a line of credit. A security analyst has been asked to assess the security risk of the minimum viable product (MVP). Which is the MOST important activity the analyst should assess?
options: The software has the correct functionality.
The software has been code reviewed.
The software had been branded according to corporate standards
The software has been signed off for release by the product owner.
questions.explanation: For security risk, the key check is whether the code has been reviewed for flaws before customer exposure; functionality, branding and sign-off are not security assurances.
optionNotes: Functional, not security
Right: code review finds security defects
Cosmetic
Business approval, not security assurance

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to protect against Structured Query language (SQL) injection?
options: Restrict HyperText Markup Language (HTML) source code
questions.explanation: Parameterized stored procedures separate code from data, so user input cannot change the SQL statement.
optionNotes: Boundary checks address buffer overflows
Impractical and ineffective
Unrelated to SQL
Right: parameterized queries/stored procedures

questions.stem: A security professional recommends that a company integrate threat modeling into its Agile development processes. Which of the following BEST describes the benefits of this approach?
options: Potential threats are addressed later in the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
Improve user acceptance of implemented security controls.
Potential threats are addressed earlier in the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
questions.explanation: Threat modeling during Agile iterations surfaces threats early, when they are cheapest to fix.
optionNotes: Possible side effect, not the main benefit
Opposite
Not the purpose
Right: shift left

questions.stem: The quality assurance (QA) department is short-staffed and is unable to test all modules before the anticipated release date of an application. What security control is MOST likely to be violated?
questions.explanation: Releasing modules that have not been tested skips a required approval and testing gate in the change management process, so that is the control violated.
optionNotes: Environments can stay separated even without testing.
Program management is broader governance, not the specific control.
Mobile code is irrelevant here.
Correct: untested changes bypass change control.

questions.stem: Which attack defines a piece of code that is inserted into software to trigger a malicious function?
questions.explanation: A logic bomb is code planted in software that triggers a malicious action when a condition is met, such as a date or an event.
optionNotes: Phishing is social engineering.
Salami attacks skim small amounts repeatedly.
A back door is a hidden access path, not a triggered payload.
Correct: a logic bomb fires on a trigger condition.

questions.stem: In what phase of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) should security training for the development team begin?
questions.explanation: Security must be built in from the start of the SDLC, and NIST SP 800-64 places security planning, including team awareness, in Initiation.
optionNotes: Training should come before development begins.
Correct: security starts at Initiation.
Too late; the code already exists.
Disposal is the end of life.

questions.stem: What is the HIGHEST priority in agile development?
options: Early and continuous delivery of software
Maximizing the amount of code delivered
questions.explanation: The first principle of the Agile Manifesto is satisfying the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software.
optionNotes: Language choice is a technical detail.
Cost matters but is not the top agile priority.
Correct: first Agile Manifesto principle.
Agile values working software, not code volume.

questions.stem: An organization purchased a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software several years ago. The information technology (IT) Director has decided to migrate the application into the cloud, but is concerned about the application security of the software in the organization's dedicated environment with a cloud service provider. What is the BEST way to prevent and correct the software's security weaknesses
options: Implement a dedicated COTS sandbox environment
Transfer the risk to the cloud service provider
Examine the software updating and patching process
questions.explanation: Security flaws in COTS software are prevented and corrected via the vendor update and patching process, which must be examined before migrating.
optionNotes: A sandbox isolates the software but does not fix its flaws.
The end-of-life schedule does not correct weaknesses.
Risk transfer neither prevents nor corrects flaws, and accountability stays.
Right: vendor patching is how COTS flaws are fixed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is fundamentally required to address potential security issues when initiating software development?
options: Implement ongoing security audits in all environments.
Ensure isolation of development from production.
Add information security objectives into development.
questions.explanation: Security must be built in from the start by including security objectives and requirements in development.
optionNotes: Audits come later, not at initiation.
Separating environments is good practice but not the fundamental starting point.
Right: security requirements built in from the start.
Code review needs code to exist first.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective preventative method to identify security flaws in software?
options: Use automated security vulnerability testing tools.
questions.explanation: A structured code review finds flaws early, before deployment, making it the most effective preventive method.
optionNotes: Monitoring production is detective, after release.
Right: a structured review finds flaws before release.
Penetration testing happens late and is not preventive.
Automated tools miss logic flaws and give false positives.

questions.stem: A software developer wishes to write code that will execute safely and only as intended. Which of the following programming language types is MOST likely to achieve this goal?
questions.explanation: Strongly typed languages prevent unintended type conversions and operations, so code behaves as intended.
optionNotes: Static typing checks at compile time but can still allow unsafe casts.
Weak typing allows implicit, unsafe conversions.
Right: strict type enforcement prevents unintended behavior.
Dynamic typing defers checks to runtime.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST method to identify security controls that should be implemented for a web-based application while in development?
questions.explanation: Threat modeling during design identifies threats and the controls needed to counter them.
optionNotes: Right: threat modeling maps threats to the controls needed.
Secure development is a general approach, not a way to identify controls.
Agile is a delivery method.
Penetration testing comes later and tests controls instead of identifying them.

questions.stem: Which of the following will help prevent improper session handling?
options: Ensure that all UlWebView calls do not execute without proper input validation.
Ensure that tokens are sufficiently long, complex, and pseudo-random.
Ensure JavaScript and plugin support is disabled.
Ensure that certificates are valid and fail closed.
questions.explanation: Session management depends on session tokens that cannot be predicted. Long, random, high-entropy tokens prevent session guessing and hijacking.
optionNotes: Input validation addresses injection, not session handling.
Correct: strong random tokens resist session prediction.
Disabling scripts is a client hardening step, not session management.
Certificate validation protects transport and the server's identity.

questions.stem: At what stage of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) does software vulnerability remediation MOST likely cost the least to implement?
questions.explanation: The earlier a flaw is fixed, the cheaper it is. Of the listed phases, design is the earliest, so addressing vulnerabilities there costs least.
optionNotes: Development comes after design, so fixes cost more.
Fixes in testing cost more still.
Fixes after deployment are the most expensive.
Correct: design is the earliest listed phase.

questions.stem: The ability to send malicious code, generally in the form of a client side script, to a different end user is categorized as which type of vulnerability?
questions.explanation: XSS injects client-side script that runs in another user's browser. That matches the description exactly.
optionNotes: Session hijacking steals sessions; it is not script delivery.
CSRF forges requests; it does not deliver script to users.
Correct: XSS delivers malicious script to other users.
Command injection runs OS commands on the server.

questions.stem: A retail company is looking to start a development project that will utilize open source components in its code for the first time. The development team has already acquired several 'open source components and utilized them in proof of concept (POC) code. The team recognizes that the legal and operational risks are outweighed by the benefits of open-source software use. What MUST the organization do next?
options: Mandate that all open-source components be approved by the Information Security Manager (ISM).
Scan all open-source components for security vulnerabilities.
Require commercial support for all open-source components.
questions.explanation: Policy comes before technology. Before using open source, the organization must set a governing policy covering licensing, approval and vulnerability management. Scanning and approvals then follow from that policy.
optionNotes: One person's approval without a policy is ad hoc.
Scanning is a control that should come from the policy.
Correct: a compliance policy governs licensing and use.
Commercial support is optional and not mandated.

questions.stem: Which of the following does the security design process ensure within the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC)?
options: Proper security controls, security goals, and fault mitigation are properly conducted.
Proper security controls, security objectives, and security goals are properly initiated.
Security goals, proper security controls, and validation are properly initiated.
Security objectives, security goals, and system test are properly conducted.
questions.explanation: In the SDLC, security design establishes the security objectives and goals and selects the right controls. Validation and testing belong to later phases.
optionNotes: Fault mitigation is not the design deliverable.
Correct: objectives, goals and controls are established during design.
Validation is a later phase.
System testing is a later phase.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective method of detecting vulnerabilities in web-based applications early in the secure Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)?
questions.explanation: Code review can happen during development, before the application runs, so it finds flaws earliest. Scanning, fuzzing and pen testing need a working build.
optionNotes: Needs a running application, so it comes later.
Needs an executable and comes later.
Correct: it is the earliest of these and finds flaws in source code.
Done late, against a deployed or test system.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the GREATEST risk of relying only on Capability Maturity Models (CMM) for software to guide process improvement and assess capabilities of acquired software?
options: Organizations can only reach a maturity level 3 when using CMMs
CMMs do not explicitly address safety and security
CMMs can only be used for software developed in-house
CMMs are vendor specific and may be biased
questions.explanation: Software CMMs measure how mature a process is, not the security or safety of the product. Relying on them alone leaves security unaddressed.
optionNotes: CMMs go up to level 5.
Correct: CMMs do not explicitly cover security or safety.
CMMs can also be used to assess suppliers.
CMMs are not vendor-specific.

questions.stem: What is the BEST control to be implemented at a login page in a web application to mitigate the ability to enumerate users?
options: Implement a generic response for a failed login attempt.
Implement a strong password during account registration.
Implement numbers and special characters in the user name.
Implement two-factor authentication (2FA) to login process.
questions.explanation: User enumeration exploits different error messages, such as 'unknown user' versus 'wrong password'. A single generic failure response removes that signal.
optionNotes: Correct: identical responses stop enumeration.
Password strength does not hide whether a user exists.
Username complexity does not stop the oracle.
2FA protects authentication but the error messages can still reveal users.

questions.stem: An attack utilizing social engineering and a malicious Uniform Resource Locator (URL) link to take advantage of a victim's existing browser session with a web application is an example of which of the following types of attack?
questions.explanation: CSRF tricks a victim, often via a link, into sending a request that rides on their existing authenticated session. That is exactly the scenario described.
optionNotes: XSS runs injected script; it does not specifically abuse an existing session.
Correct: CSRF abuses the victim's existing session.
Injection targets backend interpreters.
Clickjacking uses hidden UI overlays.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects should be removed FIRST prior to uploading code to public code repositories?
questions.explanation: Hard-coded credentials, keys or tokens in public repositories are harvested within minutes. They must be removed, and rotated, before the code is published.
optionNotes: Correct: secrets exposure is the immediate critical risk.
Should be fixed but is not the first removal.
A quality issue.
A quality issue.

questions.stem: What high Availability (HA) option of database allows multiple clients to access multiple database servers simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Replication keeps copies on multiple servers that clients can use concurrently, providing availability.
optionNotes: Data model, not HA option
Data model, not HA option
Shadow is a standby copy
Correct: multiple active servers

questions.stem: A security engineer is designing a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) application for a third-party vendor. In which phase of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) will it be MOST beneficial to conduct a data sensitivity assessment?
questions.explanation: Data sensitivity and security categorization are performed at initiation so that requirements can be built into the design.
optionNotes: Too late for requirements
Correct: early categorization
Not an SDLC phase
Far too late

questions.stem: According to the Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI), which of the following levels is identified by a managed process that is tailored from the organization's set of standard processes according to the organization's tailoring guidelines?
questions.explanation: In CMMI, level 3 (Defined) processes are tailored from the organization's standard process set.
optionNotes: Not a tailored process
Ad hoc
Project-level, not tailored from standard set
Correct: Defined level tailors from org standard process set

questions.stem: Limiting the processor, memory, and Input/output (I/O) capabilities of mobile code is known as
questions.explanation: Sandboxing confines mobile code by restricting resources it can use.
optionNotes: Not a standard term
Compilation technique
Correct: sandbox limits CPU, memory and I/O of mobile code
Separation concept, not resource limits
